definition: Naomi Sager (born 1927) is an American computational linguistics research scientist.
details: She is a former research professor at New York University, now retired. She is a pioneer in the development of natural language processing for computers.
story: Picture a translator at the United Nations, listening to one language and whispering the meaning into another in real time. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. Meaning lives in company — a word is known by the words it keeps. That pattern-earned fluency is Naomi Sager.
